video:video.video:title: Tejas Singh: A Life of Crime
video:video.video:description: Tejas Singh sings A Life of Crime and plays guitar. He builds familiar songs from the ground up with a loop pedal, and if you'd like to hear his originals, just let us know.

video:video.video:title: Tejas Singh live: acoustic singer and guitarist for private parties and weddings
video:video.video:description: This is Tejas Singh's full live set at Sofar Sounds. He sings and plays guitar, and he builds up each song by recording little parts and playing over them. He can bring the same sound to your private party or wedding cocktail hour.

video:video.video:title: Acoustic singer-songwriter for a wedding cocktail hour: Tejas Singh, Thirty Days
video:video.video:description: Tejas Singh sings Thirty Days with his acoustic guitar at a wedding cocktail hour, and he plays soft enough that guests can keep talking.

video:video.video:title: Live band for a holiday party: Tejas Singh quartet
video:video.video:description: Tejas Singh's quartet plays a holiday party with a dance floor in front of the band. The quartet is the largest group Tejas offers, and it's a great choice if you want people dancing at a holiday party or a reception.

video:video.video:title: Singer and guitarist for a private party: Tejas Singh live-looping No Woman No Cry
video:video.video:description: Tejas Singh builds No Woman No Cry from the ground up with live looping. He's one musician with a loop pedal, recording each part as he plays it, and by the second chorus he sounds like a full band.

video:video.video:title: Jazz duo for a cocktail hour: Autumn Leaves on guitar and upright bass
video:video.video:description: Here's the jazz duo playing Autumn Leaves on guitar and upright bass, at a volume that suits a cocktail hour. Book the duo when you want jazz standards playing as your guests arrive.

video:video.video:title: Jazz trio for a cocktail hour: Sunny
video:video.video:description: A jazz trio plays Sunny on guitar, upright bass and drums, and the drummer uses brushes to keep the volume down. You can book the trio for a cocktail hour, dinner or the whole event.

video:video.video:title: Flamenco trio for a private dinner: Dirty Flamenco, live
video:video.video:description: Dirty Flamenco plays traditional flamenco and rumba while guests have dinner at a private event. The trio is flamenco guitar, bass and cajón (a wooden box drum).

video:video.video:title: Flamenco guitar for a cocktail hour: tangos, Dirty Flamenco
video:video.video:description: Dirty Flamenco plays tangos, a quick, bright style of traditional flamenco, at a cocktail hour. They can keep the volume low enough for guests to talk without raising their voices.

video:video.video:title: Flamenco guitar for a garden party: Bart's rumba, Dirty Flamenco
video:video.video:description: Dirty Flamenco plays Bart's rumba at a garden party, and they can bring the volume down so your guests can keep talking.

video:video.video:title: Flamenco trio for a private party: rumba, Dirty Flamenco
video:video.video:description: The three musicians in Dirty Flamenco play a rumba on guitar, bass and percussion at a private party.

video:video.video:title: Spanish guitar for a dinner party: farruca, Dirty Flamenco
video:video.video:description: A farruca on solo Spanish guitar, played live. It's a traditional style of flamenco, and Dirty Flamenco's guitarist can play it at your dinner party or cocktail hour.

video:video.video:title: Spanish guitar for a private party: the Sabicas verdiales
video:video.video:description: A short piece by Sabicas on solo Spanish guitar, played live. If you're planning a private party, you can book Dirty Flamenco's guitarist on his own.

video:video.video:title: Spanish guitar for a wedding ceremony: Can't Help Falling in Love
video:video.video:description: Can't Help Falling in Love on solo Spanish guitar, played live. It's a popular choice for a wedding processional, and Dirty Flamenco's guitarist would love to play it at your ceremony.

video:video.video:title: Spanish guitar for a wedding ceremony: Malagueña, Dirty Flamenco
video:video.video:description: Gary Meyers plays a Malagueña on solo Spanish guitar. He's the guitarist in Dirty Flamenco, and you can book him on his own for a wedding ceremony.

video:video.video:title: Three Spanish guitars for a corporate event: Entre dos Aguas
video:video.video:description: Three flamenco guitarists take turns on Entre dos Aguas, and it makes a great feature at a corporate event. Dirty Flamenco can play as three guitars if that's the sound you want.

video:video.video:title: Dirty Flamenco, live
video:video.video:description: Here's a minute of Dirty Flamenco playing live at a private event, with flamenco guitar, bass and percussion. They're one of the few flamenco groups in Colorado.

video:video.video:title: Tony Medina as a duo: Going Down, the Freddie King standard
video:video.video:description: In this clip, Tony Medina plays the Freddie King blues standard Going Down as a duo. His song list starts with the blues of Freddie King and B.B. King, and he can play those songs on his own or with a bigger band.

video:video.video:title: Tony Medina as a duo: Don't Drink the Water, a Dave Matthews Band cover
video:video.video:description: Here's Tony Medina as a duo, playing Don't Drink the Water by the Dave Matthews Band. He can also play solo, or bring a band of up to four if you want something bigger.

video:video.video:title: Blues guitar for a private party: The Thrill Is Gone, Tony Medina
video:video.video:description: Tony Medina plays The Thrill Is Gone, the B.B. King song, live at a blues jam. His song list goes from Freddie King all the way to The Cars and Prince.

video:video.video:title: Classic rock covers for an office party: Drive, Tony Medina
video:video.video:description: Here's Tony Medina at an office party, playing Drive, the Cars song. He can play solo for welcome drinks and dinner, and he can bring a band of up to four if you want people dancing.

video:video.video:title: Singer and guitarist for welcome drinks: Tony Medina's song Headline
video:video.video:description: Tony Medina sings and plays guitar on Headline, one of his own songs. He mixes originals like this one in with his covers.

video:video.video:title: Tony Medina live: blues and rock voice and guitar for private events in Denver
video:video.video:description: Tony Medina sings Purple Rain with his acoustic guitar. You can book him in Denver for a milestone birthday, an office party or a rehearsal dinner.

video:video.video:title: René Moffatt acoustic: If You Were Near
video:video.video:description: René Moffatt plays his song If You Were Near on acoustic guitar in a Denver studio. This is what he sounds like solo, and your guests can easily talk over it.

video:video.video:title: René Moffatt covers Blackbird by The Beatles
video:video.video:description: René Moffatt plays an acoustic cover of Blackbird by The Beatles. He leads with his own songs, and he's happy to mix in covers like this one if you ask.

video:video.video:title: René Moffatt covers Willie Nelson: Mammas Don't Let Your Babies Grow Up To Be Cowboys
video:video.video:description: René Moffatt recorded this Willie Nelson song in the studio with a band behind him. If you'd like covers at your event, let us know and he can play them alongside his own songs.

video:video.video:title: René Moffatt as a trio: Heirloom Winnebago
video:video.video:description: René Moffatt plays his song Heirloom Winnebago with lead guitar and bass at an album release show in Denver. The trio gives you a fuller sound without drums.

video:video.video:title: René Moffatt and his band live: Stuck Inside
video:video.video:description: René Moffatt and his band play Stuck Inside, one of his own songs, live in Denver. Alex Dezen of The Damnwells called this song equally whimsical and profound.

video:video.video:title: René Moffatt live: an original singer-songwriter on voice and acoustic guitar, for private events in Denver
video:video.video:description: René Moffatt sings his own song Hope For Better Things with his acoustic guitar in a studio. If you're planning a ceremony or a retreat, he can bring this same sound to your event.

video:video.video:title: René Moffatt solo at a listening venue: Standing In The Shadow Of The Moon
video:video.video:description: Here's René Moffatt on his own with an acoustic guitar, singing his song Standing In The Shadow Of The Moon live at a Colorado listening venue in February 2026.

video:video.video:title: René Moffatt live: Goodnight, Texas
video:video.video:description: René Moffatt sings his song Goodnight, Texas with his acoustic guitar on stage at a Denver club in March 2026.

video:video.video:title: René Moffatt and his band live: Calendar Year
video:video.video:description: René Moffatt & The Moonshadows, his four-piece band, play his song Calendar Year on stage at a Denver club. This is a great size for a park stage or a summer party.

video:video.video:title: René Moffatt & The Moonshadows at the Underground Music Showcase: Calendar Year
video:video.video:description: René Moffatt's full band plays his song Calendar Year at the Underground Music Showcase in Denver in the summer of 2026. This is the band he can bring when you want something bigger than a solo set.

video:video.video:title: René Moffatt & The Moonshadows at the Underground Music Showcase: Come Of Age
video:video.video:description: Here's René Moffatt with his full band, playing his song Come Of Age at the Underground Music Showcase in Denver in the summer of 2026. This is his folk and Americana sound with drums and bass behind it.

video:video.video:title: René Moffatt & The Moonshadows at the Underground Music Showcase: Drive, a Cars cover
video:video.video:description: René Moffatt and his full band cover Drive by The Cars at the Underground Music Showcase in Denver in the summer of 2026. They played it in a set of his own songs.

video:video.video:title: René Moffatt & The Moonshadows at the Underground Music Showcase: Goodnight, Texas
video:video.video:description: René Moffatt & The Moonshadows play his song Goodnight, Texas at the Underground Music Showcase in Denver in the summer of 2026. This is the one to book when you want his own songs with a full band behind them.

video:video.video:title: René Moffatt & The Moonshadows at the Underground Music Showcase: Halfway Home
video:video.video:description: René Moffatt & The Moonshadows play his song Halfway Home at the Underground Music Showcase in Denver in summer 2026. You can book the same band for your event, too.

video:video.video:title: René Moffatt & The Moonshadows at the Underground Music Showcase: Iron Gates Of Love
video:video.video:description: René Moffatt wrote Iron Gates Of Love, and in summer 2026 he played it with his full band at the Underground Music Showcase in Denver. He's a lot louder with the band behind him than he is in his solo sets.

video:video.video:title: René Moffatt & The Moonshadows at the Underground Music Showcase: Stuck Inside
video:video.video:description: This is René Moffatt's full band, The Moonshadows, playing his song Stuck Inside on the Underground Music Showcase stage in Denver in the summer of 2026. For a dinner, he can also play solo with just his voice and an acoustic guitar.

video:video.video:title: René Moffatt & The Moonshadows at the Underground Music Showcase: Waterfall
video:video.video:description: In summer 2026, René Moffatt played his song Waterfall with his full band at the Underground Music Showcase in Denver. This is how the band sounds at festival volume, and we can size the sound system to suit your venue.

video:video.video:title: René Moffatt & The Moonshadows at the Underground Music Showcase: What If I, What If You
video:video.video:description: Here's one of René Moffatt's own songs, What If I, What If You, played by his full band in summer 2026 at the Underground Music Showcase in Denver.

video:video.video:title: Solo jazz guitar for a cocktail hour: a blues in the style of Grant Green
video:video.video:description: This is a blues in the style of the jazz guitarist Grant Green, played on one guitar at a level where your guests can keep talking. One guitarist is our smallest live option, and it's a great choice for a cocktail hour or a dinner.

video:video.video:title: Solo jazz guitarist for a client dinner: Autumn Leaves
video:video.video:description: This is Autumn Leaves on one guitar, quiet enough to talk over, and a solo guitarist works well for a smaller group. The guitarist only needs a small corner of your venue, too.

video:video.video:title: Acoustic singer and guitarist for a private party: Mary Jane's Last Dance
video:video.video:description: One musician sings and plays Mary Jane's Last Dance, the Tom Petty song, at a private party. You can book a singer and guitarist for just an hour, or from the time your guests arrive through dinner.

video:video.video:title: Solo jazz guitar for a holiday party: White Christmas
video:video.video:description: One jazz guitarist plays White Christmas here, at a volume that suits a holiday dinner. That's our smallest Christmas option. We can play the same song list as a trio by adding upright bass and drums played softly with brushes.

video:video.video:title: String quartet for a gala or a wedding: Beethoven's Op. 18 No. 6, first two movements
video:video.video:description: A string quartet of two violins, viola and cello plays the first two movements of Beethoven's Op. 18 No. 6, and you can hear how full the sound gets with all four players.

video:video.video:title: Solo violin for a wedding ceremony: the Andante from Bach's Sonata No. 2
video:video.video:description: This is the Andante, a slow movement from Bach's second sonata for solo violin, played by one violinist with no accompaniment. It's a lovely choice for the prelude or the processional at a wedding ceremony.

video:video.video:title: Solo violin: Paganini's Caprice No. 19
video:video.video:description: Here's Paganini's Caprice No. 19 in E-flat major, played on a single violin. This is the kind of piece you'd hear at a concert, and our string players can also play Bach at your wedding ceremony or Coldplay arranged for strings.

video:video.video:title: Solo violin: the Allegro from Bach's Sonata No. 2
video:video.video:description: A violinist plays the Allegro from Bach's second sonata for solo violin. One violinist is a great choice for a wedding ceremony or a dinner, and we can add players all the way up to a full string quartet.

video:video.video:title: Violin: the first movement of the Sibelius Violin Concerto
video:video.video:description: Here’s the Allegro moderato, the opening movement of the Sibelius Violin Concerto in D minor, Op. 47. It’s a thirteen-minute concert piece played by a violinist from our string quartet.

video:video.video:title: Afro house DJ for an after-party: live DJ set
video:video.video:description: Here’s the DJ playing a live outdoor set. The DJ plays Afro house, deep house, amapiano, techno and electronic music, and can play live tabla on request.
